title: Proximity-induced charge density waves in a moiré heterobilayer
authors: Christopher T. S. Cheung, Arash A. Mostofi, Johannes Lischner
abstract: Twisted heterobilayers of two-dimensional materials have emerged as a platform for studying emergent phases of matter. In this work, we investigate charge density waves (CDW) in a twisted NbSe$_2$/MoSe$_2$ bilayer using first-principles calculations. We observe CDW formation in both layers, even though MoSe$_2$ does not feature a CDW in its monolayer form. Moreover, we find that the CDW is highly non-uniform with filled-center, hollow-center and hexagonal CDWs coexisting in the moiré unit cells of both layers. We assess different mechanisms of CDW formation in the MoSe$_2$ layer and conclude that the dominant one is the steric repulsion between Se atoms across the van der Waals gap. The strength of this effect is highly sensitive to the interlayer separation, which explains why the CDW amplitude in the MoSe$_2$ layer depends strongly on the local stacking arrangement. Our work demonstrates that novel broken-symmetry phases can be induced in twisted heterobilayers through proximity effects.
summary: This work uses first-principles calculations to study Charge Density Waves in a twisted $	ext{NbSe}_2/	ext{MoSe}_2$ heterobilayer. It finds that the $	ext{MoSe}_2$ layer develops a CDW due to steric repulsion from the neighboring layer, even though it is absent in its monolayer form. This highlights how interlayer interactions can induce novel, symmetry-broken electronic phases in 2D materials.
main_problem: The study investigates the formation and nature of Charge Density Waves (CDWs) in twisted heterobilayers, specifically focusing on proximity-induced CDW effects.
main_result: CDW formation is observed in both layers ($	ext{NbSe}_2$ and $	ext{MoSe}_2$), with the $	ext{MoSe}_2$ CDW being driven by steric repulsion across the van der Waals gap, demonstrating novel broken-symmetry phases.
method: The research employs first-principles calculations (DFT) to analyze the smeared atomic density and identify coexisting CDW types using phase field analysis.
model_or_system: The physical system is a twisted $	ext{NbSe}_2/	ext{MoSe}_2$ heterobilayer. The analysis examines how the moiré superlattice structure influences electronic instabilities.
key_observables: Smeared atomic density modulation, CDW types (filled-center, hollow-center, hexagonal), and the CDW displacement amplitude ($ ar{v}$).
important_parameters: Interlayer separation and local stacking arrangement, which strongly modulate the CDW amplitude.
main_assumptions: The CDW modulation can be described by a Fourier series, and the dominant mechanism in $	ext{MoSe}_2$ is attributed to steric repulsion.
figures_summary: Figures show smeared densities revealing CDW modulation in both layers, illustrating the co-existence of different CDW types in the twisted bilayer, and quantifying the linear dependence of the induced CDW amplitude on the fixed CDW amplitude.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the CDW formation in the bilayer, first establishing the general CDW diagnostics, then detailing the specific mechanism (steric repulsion) responsible for the proximity effect in the $	ext{MoSe}_2$ layer, and finally quantifying the dependence on stacking.
why_interesting: The concept of proximity-induced symmetry breaking and emergent electronic phases in van der Waals heterostructures is highly relevant to understanding tunable quantum materials systems.
